## Updated cost:benefit ranking (win-projects-from-Semgrep/CodeQL lens, measured)

| # | Item | Benefit (measured) | Cost |
|---|------|--------------------|------|
| 1 | **#2354** — authored servlet-request source summaries | **1,192 cases (76% of corpus)** blocked at `getParameter`-style external interface calls | Pack content + one gated experiment |
| 2 | **#2355** — bakeoff policy-set sink/source gaps | 320 cases (20%) never form a root | Small (policy content) |
| 3 | **#2356** — xss `InternalInvariant` + witness projection loss | Report integrity for the largest category; direct finding loss | Small-medium defect |
| 4 | **Honest-completion path** (#1877/#1869/#1868 + #2354) | Honest J is 0.000 — *nothing* concludes Complete; this is the differentiator claim | Medium (evidence plumbing over #2354's content) |
| 5 | **#2276** — implicit abort-edge lowering | 60 cases + true-negative conclusions everywhere | Large, fully specified |
| 6 | **#2277 re-measure** | Unknown until #2354 lands (measured null twice, upstream-blocked) | Trivial (one A/B after #2354) |
| 7 | **#1871 demand sweep rerun** | Its blocker (framework types) is now #2354's exact scope | Small after #2354 |

Reasoning on the big calls:

1. **#2354 is the whole game now.** Three-quarters of the corpus abstains at one mechanism, and the probe corpus proves the engine completes equivalent flows when the source isn't an external interface method. This is #1871/#1877's "library models are the moat" thesis showing up as a scoreboard number. It's also the one item with a real false-green hazard — an authored-complete request summary is the first place Bifrost could clear a vulnerable case — so the experiment must gate on false-greens-stay-0 before anything ships as default.
2. **#2355 is the cheapest 20% you'll ever buy** — the bakeoff's own sink/source sets miss `JdbcTemplate` and friends. Worth doing before #2354 so the summary experiment measures against a corpus that can actually bind.
3. **The honest-score gap (rank 4) is the marketing-critical one**: naive J now exists, but the "honest, no-false-greens" pitch needs cases reaching `Complete`/`ProvenBySummary`, which is the same substrate as #2354 plus completion evidence. Until then the differentiator is asserted, not demonstrated.
4. Items that fell off the list: budget/charging work (all walls down, six of them), CHA expansion (measured null twice — cheap to re-test, wrong to invest in now), and everything in the residual chain (empty).

Rough sequencing that maximizes slope: #2355 → #2354 experiment (false-green-gated) → re-run bakeoff + #2277 A/B + #1871 sweep in one session → then decide between #2276 and the honest-completion plumbing with fresh numbers.Stopping condition reached — everything left is content or design work, not an obvious defect.
